title: SPARK CSEC Mathematics - Paper 02 Practice Paper A
instructions: This paper consists of THREE sections: I, II and III.
Section I has THREE questions; Section II has THREE questions and Section III has THREE questions.
Numerical answers that are non-exact should be given correct to 3 significant figures or 1 decimal place for angles in degrees, unless a different level of accuracy is specified in the question.
All working MUST be clearly shown.
A table of formulae is provided.

parts.label: (b) (ii)

parts.label: (c) (i)
parts.prompt:
Kalifa's mobile telephone plan has a fixed charge of $45.00 per month, which includes 300 minutes of calls. Each additional minute is charged at $0.35. In January she made calls totalling 465 minutes.

Calculate the TOTAL amount that Kalifa paid for her telephone service for the month of January.
parts.solution: Kalifa made 465 - 300 = 165 minutes of calls beyond those included, and these cost 165 x $0.35 = $57.75. The total amount paid is $45.00 + $57.75 = $102.75.

criteria.description: finding the charge for the 165 additional minutes
the total amount paid

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: For the next month, February, Kalifa paid $136.00 for her telephone service. Determine the TOTAL number of minutes of calls that she made in February.
parts.solution: The charge for the additional minutes was $136.00 - $45.00 = $91.00, so the number of additional minutes is 91.00/0.35 = 260. Adding the 300 minutes included in the plan, Kalifa made 300 + 260 = 560 minutes of calls.

criteria.description: subtracting the fixed charge and dividing by the charge per additional minute
the total number of minutes

questions.stem: Anisha is investigating the sums of sequences of whole numbers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Anisha first added the odd numbers, starting at 1: the first 2 odd numbers, then the first 3, then the first 4, and so on. The first rows of the table are shown below. Some rows have not been included.

Study the pattern of numbers in each row of the table. Complete the table by filling in the missing information.
parts.solution: Each row adds the next odd number. The nth odd number is 2n - 1, so the 5th is 2(5) - 1 = 9 and the 9th is 2(9) - 1 = 17. The sum of the first n odd numbers is n^2, so the sum of the first 4 is 4^2 = 16, of the first 5 is 5^2 = 25, and of the first 9 is 9^2 = 81.

table.caption: The sums of the odd numbers.

s4.description: the sum of the first 4 odd numbers

s5.description: the sum of the first 5 odd numbers

s9.description: the sum of the first 9 odd numbers

ln.description: the nth odd number, in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
Anisha then added the EVEN numbers in the same way, and noted that

2 + 4 = 6 = 2 x 3
2 + 4 + 6 = 12 = 3 x 4
2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20 = 4 x 5.

Using the pattern derived from the 3 statements above, determine the value of 2 + 4 + 6 + ... + 30.
parts.solution: The last number 30 is the 15th even number, and the pattern gives the sum as 15 x 16 = 240.

criteria.description: recognises that 30 is the 15th even number
the sum, 240

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Hence, write a formula in terms of n for the sum 2 + 4 + 6 + ... + 2n.
parts.solution: Each statement is of the form n(n + 1), where 2n is the last number added. So 2 + 4 + 6 + ... + 2n = n(n + 1).

criteria.description: the formula in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
A school canteen in Kingston sells patties and bottles of juice. On Monday it sold 45 patties and 30 bottles of juice, and on Tuesday it sold 52 patties and 25 bottles of juice.

Write a 2 x 2 matrix, S, to represent this information, using the rows for Monday and Tuesday and the columns for patties and juices.
parts.solution: The two rows are Monday and Tuesday and the two columns are patties and juices, so S = [[45, 30], [52, 25]].

criteria.description: the matrix S

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt:
A patty costs JA$120.00 and a bottle of juice costs JA$45.00.

Write a 2 x 1 matrix, C, to represent the cost, in Jamaican dollars, of one patty and of one bottle of juice.
parts.solution: C is a column matrix with one entry for each of the two items, in the same order as the columns of S, so C = [[120], [45]].

criteria.description: the matrix C, with the correct rows and columns

parts.label: (b) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the matrix product SC.
parts.solution: SC = [[45, 30], [52, 25]][[120], [45]]. Multiplying the first row of S by the column C gives (45 x 120) + (30 x 45) = 5400 + 1350 = 6750, and the second row gives (52 x 120) + (25 x 45) = 6240 + 1125 = 7365. So SC = [[6750], [7365]].

criteria.description: multiplying each row of S by the column C
the matrix product SC

parts.label: (b) (iv)
parts.prompt: What does the matrix product SC represent?
parts.answer: SC represents the total amount of money, in Jamaican dollars, collected from these sales on each day: JA$6750 on Monday and JA$7365 on Tuesday
parts.solution: The first row of SC is (45 x 120) + (30 x 45), the cost of Monday's patties added to the cost of Monday's juices. So SC represents the total amount of money collected from these sales on each day: JA$6750 on Monday and JA$7365 on Tuesday.

rubric.description: says that SC gives the total amount collected from these sales on each day

questions.topic: Geometric construction and trigonometry in right-angled triangles

parts.label: (a) (i)
parts.prompt:
The line AB, 8 cm long, is drawn on the construction pad.

Using only a ruler and a pair of compasses, construct triangle ABC in which AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 10 cm. Your construction arcs must be clearly shown.
parts.answer: triangle ABC with AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 10 cm, with the two arcs that locate C left on the page
parts.solution: AB = 8 cm is already drawn. Open the compasses to 10 cm and, with centre A, draw an arc above AB. Without changing the drawing, open the compasses to 6 cm and, with centre B, draw a second arc to cut the first at C. Join AC and BC with the ruler. The two arcs must be left on the page: they are the mark for the construction, and an accurate triangle measured out with a ruler alone does not earn it.

parts.label: (a) (ii)
parts.prompt: State, giving a reason for your answer, the size of angle ABC in your construction.
parts.answer: Angle ABC = 90°, because 6^2 + 8^2 = 36 + 64 = 100 = 10^2, so by the converse of Pythagoras' theorem the angle opposite AC is a right angle
parts.solution: The three sides are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, and 6^2 + 8^2 = 36 + 64 = 100, which is 10^2. By the converse of Pythagoras' theorem, the angle opposite the longest side AC is a right angle, so angle ABC = 90°.

rubric.description: states 90 degrees and gives Pythagoras' theorem as the reason

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The diagram below shows a right-angled triangle PQR, in which PQ = 12 cm, QR = 5 cm and angle PQR = 90°.

Determine the length of PR.
parts.solution: By Pythagoras' theorem, PR^2 = PQ^2 + QR^2 = 12^2 + 5^2 = 144 + 25 = 169. So PR = sqrt(169) = 13 cm.

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Derive a simplified expression for g^(-1)(x).

Collecting the terms in y on one side gives xy - 2y = 4x + 3, that is y(x - 2) = 4x + 3. Dividing by x - 2 gives g^(-1)(x) = (4x + 3)/(x - 2).

the correct inverse

parts.solution: Each cumulative frequency is the running total of the frequencies up to and including that class: 4, 15, 36, 52, 60. So the two missing values are 36 and 52.
